## Decision record: what the rank-selection face promises, and what its receipts look like

::: {.callout .callout-note}
**Decision.** CS-20 is a witness, not a specification: it freezes what the
exported `ms_select_k()` generic actually adjudicates over planted catalogs,
so future drift speaks immediately. It commits only machine-stable facts: the
error CLASS always, and the message CLAUSES verbatim -- every one of them. The
face runs a THREE-LAYER arbitration -- a SUITOR cross-validation argmin, a
stability veto over per-signature consensus, and a Wilcoxon diagnostic that
never decides -- and returns a PLAIN LIST (`k`, `k_evidence`), not an S7
container, so the accepted render commits the list's structural identity
instead of a class token. The evidence frame is fifteen columns wide; because
the shipped face leaves `n_seeds_converged` a documented placeholder
(`NA_integer_`), the render speaks that column as a structural `N` glyph and
never as a converged-seed integer. Under the D11 cross-platform posture every
committed arm is integer, label, logical, class or clause bytes: the accepted
arms commit the rank echo, the fifteen-column schema, the
`is_argmin`/`passes_veto`/`selected` logical glyphs and a digit-scrubbed
`veto_reason`, never a float payload. The lane also reproduced, live, the
face's gate ORDER: the dots sweep fires ahead of the dispatch check, the
dispatch check ahead of the `cv` gate, and the `cv` gate ahead of both the
grid-shape and `k_folds` laws.
:::

### The face

`ms_select_k(catalog, k_grid, replicates = 8L, max_iter = 200L, seed = 1, k_folds = 10L, n_seeds = 10L, cv = TRUE, threads = NULL, ...)`
is the exported S7 generic (`R/kselect-select.R:1`) that picks the number of
mutational signatures to decompose into. It is a dispatcher on `catalog`
(`MsCatalog`), and for each rank in `k_grid` it runs the Rust NMF pipeline,
assembles a fifteen-column evidence frame, and hands that frame to the
three-layer arbitrator. The generic measures 449 lines; the arbitration
constants are frozen (`.MS_VETO_AVG_MIN <- 0.8`,
`.MS_VETO_CLUSTER_MIN <- 0.2`, `.MS_VETO_SUM_MIN <- 1.0`). CS-20 fires 36
observation arms at it plus four boundary-pair rows: 8 law arms, 8 acceptance
specs, 12 precedence discriminators, 8 degenerate rows (4 pairs), 16 scalars.
The committed lane replays every arm live: the law file adjudicates 273
expectations across 10 units (0 failed, 0 errors, 0 skipped, 0 warnings) and
the runner rails every row against the frozen block before any witness byte is
written.

### The three arbitration layers -- and why the placeholder glyph matters

The face decides a rank by walking three layers and returning the first that
speaks. **Layer one** is the SUITOR cross-validation argmin: the lowest
`cv_test_deviance` wins, and a tie is broken by the lowest rank -- this is the
`is_argmin` glyph. **Layer two** is the stability veto: a rank survives only
if `avg_stability >= 0.8` AND `min_cluster_stability >= 0.2` AND
`avg_stability + min_cluster_stability >= 1.0`; this is the `passes_veto` glyph
and, where no rank survives, the `msuiter_error_kselect` abort that names the
per-rank veto reasons. **Layer three** is a Wilcoxon contrast against the
previous rank -- a DIAGNOSTIC only, committed as
`wilcoxon_p_vs_prev`/`wilcoxon_l2_median_delta` but never allowed to decide.
The `cv = FALSE` arm demotes layer one entirely: the argmin glyph goes
all-zero while layers two and three keep their verdict, and the
`cv_test_deviance`/`is_test` columns null out. The lane also commits WHY the
render carries a glyph rather than a number. The shipped face leaves
`n_seeds_converged` a placeholder -- `ev$n_seeds_converged <- NA_integer_`
(`R/kselect-select.R:169`), documented as such in the roxygen at `:294` -- so
the render's `nseeds` field is structurally all-`N`. The unit that u8 backs
asserts the glyph carries no digit at all, so a future wiring of the real
converged-seed count reddens the lane (which is the point: the witness records
the shipped contract, and the shipped contract is a placeholder).

### The laws the face demonstrates

- **The dots law.** An unknown argument refuses first as
  `msuiter_error_input` -- "unknown argument passed to ms_select_k()" -- with
  the "no passthrough arguments" bullet, the offending name, and the
  `?ms_select_k` spelling remedy. This gate sits AHEAD of dispatch, so the
  precedence ladder starts here.
- **The grid laws.** A non-numeric grid ("k_grid must be positive whole
  numbers", naming the received value and a `k_grid = k:k` example) and an
  all-zero grid (the same clause, naming the offenders) refuse as
  `msuiter_error_input`; a grid whose maximum exceeds the channel bound refuses
  -- "every k in k_grid must not exceed min(channels, samples) = k" -- naming
  the offending ranks, the total, and the `catalog has C channels x S samples`
  arithmetic, because a rank-k NMF needs `k <= min(nrow, ncol)`.
- **The dispatch law.** A `catalog` that is not an `MsCatalog` refuses --
  "catalog must be an MsCatalog object" -- naming the received class and the
  `ms_tally()` remedy. This is the `S7::class_any` fallback, and it fires
  ahead of every value law.
- **The `cv` law.** A `cv` that is not a single `TRUE`/`FALSE` refuses --
  "cv must be a single TRUE or FALSE" -- naming the received value and both
  legal forms, because `cv` switches the layer-one argmin on or off. This gate
  fires ahead of both the grid-shape law and the `k_folds` law.
- **The `k_folds` law.** A fold count above the channel count refuses --
  "k_folds must not exceed the channel count (C)" -- naming the fold count and
  the catalog's channels, because every fold must hold out at least one row per
  column (the SUITOR precondition).
- **The undecidable law.** A grid on which no rank clears the layer-two veto
  refuses as `msuiter_error_kselect` -- "K selection is undecidable: no rank in
  the grid passes the stability veto" -- naming the layer and its three frozen
  thresholds, then the per-rank reasons verbatim, and attaching the
  `k_evidence` table on the condition.
- **Precedence.** Twelve discriminators, each with its fires anchor pinned
  PRESENT and its anti anchor pinned ABSENT in the same live message: dispatch
  outranks the dots sweep, the dots sweep outranks the grid-shape law,
  dispatch outranks `cv`, `cv` outranks the grid-shape law, `cv` outranks
  `k_folds`, and the grid-bound law outranks `k_folds`.
- **The acceptance specs.** The canonical render commits the plain-list
  container (`list|k,k_evidence`), the chosen rank, the fifteen-column schema
  in order, the rank echo, the three logical glyphs, the placeholder `N` seeds,
  the fold lengths and the digit-scrubbed veto reasons. A single-rank grid
  commits one row of degenerate one-glyph fields; a saturated grid commits
  eight rows; argument order is permutation-invariant; and the unsorted and
  duplicate grids normalise to the ascending rank echo.

### The receipts

| receipt | committed bytes |
|---|---|
| `cs20_laws.tsv` | 8 arms: class split `msuiter_error_input` (7) and `msuiter_error_kselect` (1, the undecidable floor), every clause verbatim, every mode `reject` |
| `cs20_specs.tsv` | 8 accepted arms: class `list` plus the full render (the container, the chosen rank, the fifteen-column schema, the rank echo, the argmin/veto/selected glyphs, the placeholder-seed glyph, the fold lengths, the scrubbed veto reasons) |
| `cs20_precedence.tsv` | 12 discriminators, each with its fires anchor PRESENT and its anti anchor ABSENT in the live message |
| `cs20_degenerates.tsv` | 4 boundary pairs (8 rows): the passing-arbitration floor against the veto-undecidable abort, the boundary-reaching grid against the over-bound refusal, the dispatched catalog against the undispatchable one, and the two clause heads that reject at opposite ends of the ladder -- hi and lo committed side by side |
| `cs20_scalars.tsv` | 16 keys: the abort class, the dispatch class, the kselect class, the chosen rank, the evidence shape (`rows`, `cols`), the grid echo, the three logical glyphs, the evidence names and classes, the passing veto reason, the placeholder-seed glyph, and both RNG-purity rails |

The 36-row class census (`list=11`, `msuiter_error_input=23`,
`msuiter_error_kselect=2`, over the four committing rosters) is recomputed from
the frozen vectors inside the law file -- a silent class shift reddens the
lane, not the reader. All five witnesses byte-reproduce on consecutive runner
invocations, the plant and spec corpora hash identically under BOTH governed
SHA-256 kernels (`.ms_fit_sha256` and digest), the RNG-purity rails read
`FALSE` before and after, and the lane never calls the benchmark driver, the
declined calibration family, the registry face or any validator internal
(banned words, grepped over the runner source).

### The single-source build, and the audit that became the minter

Both hosts -- law file and runner -- carry one byte-identical frozen block and
one byte-identical shared code block, each injected from a single source
between BEGIN/END markers; the splice rail demands the exact marker counts and
compares the two regions across the files byte for byte. The minter IS the
audit: every one of the 36 roster arms is re-fired LIVE through the face
against the audited probe ledger; each of the 12 precedence-path arms carries
an explicit decision-record path whose FIRES/ANTI alignment is asserted
order-invariantly; every scalar is re-fireable and re-fired; and a final
RE-AUDIT re-sources the EMITTED block into a cleared namespace and re-compares
every committed literal against the ledger -- so emitter drift, chunking drift
and quoting drift all die at mint time, not at read time. The committed clause
bytes in this page are read from the committed witnesses, never re-typed from
plan.

### What the lane-building itself caught (the honest section)

The live replay killed three would-be-innocent readings before one witness
byte was trusted. First, the shared verdict helper passed the evaluation
WRAPPER (`list(ok = TRUE, v = <result>)`) to the render function, which expects
the raw `ms_select_k()` result -- so every accepted render collapsed to
`list|ok,v|||||||||` and the specs census died on a byte-drift stop. The law
block had passed only because every law arm takes the (correct) error branch;
the fix was to unwrap `r$v` in the accept branch. The frozen spec table was
already correct as minted -- the minter had always passed `r$v` -- so the
defect was in the hand-authored shared block alone, which is exactly what the
single-source discipline is meant to isolate. Second, the grid-bound
discriminator was authored against a head string that dropped the trailing
` = #`: the real message's first bullet is
"every k in k_grid must not exceed min(channels, samples) = k" (with the
bound interpolated), and `head1()` splits on `" | "`, so the expected string
had to carry the interpolation marker. Third, the dual-kernel corpus floor for
the spec roster was copied verbatim from CS-19's thirteen-arm roster and read
`100L`; the CS-20 spec corpus is 99 bytes, so the floor was lowered to `80L` --
the floor exists to catch an emptied roster, not to pin a glyph style. All
three findings were caught by the lane's own rails, before any witness byte was
committed.

### Provenance

The frozen block and the shared code block in both hosts are minted
mechanically from the audited probe ledger (audit green: 36 arms byte-exact on
live re-fire, 8 degen rows, 12/12 fires-and-anti anchors, 16 scalars re-fired);
neither is ever hand-edited in place. The plants' canonical texts hash to the
committed dual-kernel checksum
(`plant_sha256=5a46b5eb84ff8c5c...`, `spec_sha256=275580013e63e69f...`);
reifying the lane reproduces every witness byte for byte. Differentiation from
CS-19 (the comparison face): CS-19 adjudicated a three-protocol similarity
kernel whose accepted arms return real similarity matrices and whose refusals
split across two S7 gates; CS-20 adjudicates a three-LAYER arbitration that
returns a plain list rather than a container -- the first witness in the series
whose accepted render commits a structural list identity instead of a class
token, and the first that commits a documented PLACEHOLDER column
(the all-`N` seed glyph) as a frozen contract rather than waiting for the
column to be wired.

### Gate forensics

The scenarios leg for this lane (the nineteenth) was render-verified before
the full local burn. The T0 seal moved 628 -> 629 with the generator's refusal
witnessed verbatim (the DEFECT line naming 629 against the sealed 628, run
against the freshly re-weighted shard roster) before the deliberate re-seal,
per the budget law; the reified manifest carries the new law file on the T0
tier, byte-deterministic on re-mint.
